4. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - Proofs
5. //
6. // Proof functions for the abstract pool model. Each lemma encodes a caller
7. // expectation from `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-bump-allocator/caller_analysis.md`.
8. 
9. verus! {
10. 
11. //==================================================================================================
12. // Arithmetic helper
13. //==================================================================================================
14. 
15. /// If `base` and `stride` are both multiples of `m > 0`, then so is
16. /// `base + i * stride` for any `i`. Backs the per-slot alignment guarantee
17. /// (`slot_addr(i) = base + i * stride`).
18. proof fn lemma_aligned_sum(base: int, stride: int, i: int, m: int)
19.     requires
20.         m > 0,
21.         base % m == 0,
22.         stride % m == 0,
23.     ensures
24.         (base + i * stride) % m == 0,
25. {
26.     vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::lemma_fundamental_div_mod(base, m);
27.     vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::lemma_fundamental_div_mod(stride, m);
28.     let b = base / m;
29.     let s = stride / m;
30.     assert(base == m * b);
31.     assert(stride == m * s);
32.     assert(base + i * stride == (b + i * s) * m) by (nonlinear_arith)
33.         requires
34.             base == m * b,
35.             stride == m * s,
36.     ;
37.     vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::lemma_mod_multiples_basic(b + i * s, m);
38. }
39. 
40. //==================================================================================================
41. // Geometry lemmas (uniqueness / in-bounds / alignment)
42. //==================================================================================================
43. 
44. /// A well-formed pool satisfies all three geometric guarantees: every slot is
45. /// `unit_align`-aligned, lies fully inside the backing region, and is distinct
46. /// from every other slot.
47. ///
48. /// Backs caller invariants: *Alignment*, *In-bounds*, *Uniqueness / non-aliasing*.
49. pub proof fn lemma_geometry(v: BumpView)
50.     requires
51.         v.inv(),
52.     ensures
53.         v.geometry_ok(),
54. {
55.     let m = v.unit_align as int;
56.     let stride = v.stride as int;
57.     let base = v.base;
58.     let cap = v.capacity as int;
59.     let usz = v.unit_size as int;
60. 
61.     assert forall|i: int| 0 <= i < cap implies #[trigger] v.slot_addr(i) % m == 0 by {
62.         lemma_aligned_sum(base, stride, i, m);
63.     }
64. 
65.     assert forall|i: int| 0 <= i < cap implies {
66.         &&& v.base <= #[trigger] v.slot_addr(i)
67.         &&& v.slot_addr(i) + (v.unit_size as int) <= v.base + (v.storage_size as int)
68.     } by {
69.         assert(i * stride >= 0) by (nonlinear_arith)
70.             requires
71.                 i >= 0,
72.                 stride >= 0,
73.         ;
74.         assert(i * stride <= (cap - 1) * stride) by (nonlinear_arith)
75.             requires
76.                 i <= cap - 1,
77.                 stride >= 0,
78.         ;
79.         assert((cap - 1) * stride + stride == cap * stride) by (nonlinear_arith);
80.     }
81. 
82.     assert forall|i: int, j: int| (0 <= i < cap && 0 <= j < cap && i != j) implies (
83.     #[trigger] v.slot_addr(i)) != (#[trigger] v.slot_addr(j)) by {
84.         assert(v.slot_addr(i) == base + i * stride);
85.         assert(v.slot_addr(j) == base + j * stride);
86.         assert(v.slot_addr(i) - v.slot_addr(j) == (i - j) * stride) by (nonlinear_arith)
87.             requires
88.                 v.slot_addr(i) == base + i * stride,
89.                 v.slot_addr(j) == base + j * stride,
90.         ;
91.         assert((i - j) * stride != 0) by (nonlinear_arith)
92.             requires
93.                 i != j,
94.                 stride > 0,
95.         ;
96.     }
97. }
98. 
99. //==================================================================================================
100. // Capacity / transition lemmas (monotone capacity, no spurious consumption)
101. //==================================================================================================
102. 
103. /// The exhaustion boundary is exactly `allocated == capacity`: the pool has a free
104. /// slot iff fewer than `capacity` slots have been handed out.
105. ///
106. /// Backs caller invariant: *Monotone capacity* (the `Exhausted` boundary).
107. pub proof fn lemma_exhausted_boundary(v: BumpView)
108.     requires
109.         v.inv(),
110.     ensures
111.         !v.has_capacity() <==> v.allocated == v.capacity,
112. {
113. }
114. 
115. /// A successful allocation advances the cursor by exactly one slot and preserves
116. /// the invariant. The freshly handed-out index `v.allocated` was previously free
117. /// and becomes consumed.
118. ///
119. /// Backs caller invariants: *Monotone capacity* (advance by one), *Uniqueness*
120. /// (each index handed out at most once).
121. pub proof fn lemma_alloc_transition(v: BumpView)
122.     requires
123.         v.inv(),
124.         v.has_capacity(),
125.     ensures
126.         v.spec_alloc().inv(),
127.         v.spec_alloc().allocated == v.allocated + 1,
128.         !v.is_consumed(v.allocated as int),
129.         v.spec_alloc().is_consumed(v.allocated as int),
130.         // Configuration (everything except `allocated`) is unchanged.
131.         v.spec_alloc() == (BumpView { allocated: v.spec_alloc().allocated, ..v }),
132. {
133.     assert(v.spec_alloc() =~= (BumpView { allocated: v.spec_alloc().allocated, ..v }));

4. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains the abstract View (`BumpView`), its invariant and geometry
7. // helpers, the numeric specification of `align_up`, and the proof-lemma targets

25. // `usize::div_ceil` rounds the quotient towards positive infinity. It panics on a
26. // zero divisor, hence the `y != 0` precondition. For unsigned operands the result
27. // never overflows, and equals `ceil(x / y) == (x + y - 1) / y`.
28. pub assume_specification [ <usize>::div_ceil ](x: usize, y: usize) -> (result: usize)
29.     requires
30.         y != 0,
31.     ensures
32.         result as int == (x as int + y as int - 1) / (y as int),
33. ;
34. 
35. //==================================================================================================
36. // align_up - numeric specification
37. //==================================================================================================
38. 
39. /// Ghost constant: the stable base address revealed by a backend `S`'s
40. /// `as_mut_ptr()`. Uninterpreted because a static's address is opaque to Verus.
41. pub uninterp spec fn base_of<S: ?Sized>() -> int;
42. 
43. /// Abstract address of a freshly handed-out slot reference.
44. ///
45. /// Uninterpreted: a Verus `&mut T` reference carries no spec-readable address
46. /// (only raw pointers expose `.addr()`), so — mirroring `raw-array`'s uninterpreted
47. /// `view(&self) -> Seq<T>` — the address a caller observes for a returned slot is
48. /// modeled abstractly. `alloc`/`alloc_as` assert their alignment and in-bounds
49. /// guarantees over `slot_ref_addr(slot)`.
50. pub uninterp spec fn slot_ref_addr<T: ?Sized>(r: &T) -> int;
51. 
52. /// Least multiple of `alignment` that is `>= value`; `None` when `alignment == 0`
53. /// or when that multiple does not fit in a `usize`.
54. ///
55. /// This is the View-independent numeric meaning of `align_up`. The allocator's
56. /// `stride` (see `BumpView::inv`) is pinned to this function.
57. pub open spec fn align_up_spec(value: nat, alignment: nat) -> Option<nat> {
58.     if alignment == 0 {
59.         None
60.     } else {
61.         let m: int = ((value + alignment - 1) / (alignment as int)) * (alignment as int);
62.         if m > usize::MAX as int {
63.             None
64.         } else {
65.             Some(m as nat)
66.         }
67.     }
68. }
69. 
70. //==================================================================================================
71. // BumpView - abstract pool model
72. //==================================================================================================
73. 
74. /// Abstract view of a `FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>`.
75. ///
76. /// Pure ghost description of the slot pool: no atomics, no raw pointers, no cursor
77. /// mechanism. Carries the fixed pool geometry plus the single dynamic quantity
78. /// `allocated` (the number of slots handed out so far).
79. #[verifier::ext_equal]
80. pub struct BumpView {
81.     /// Base address of the backing region (`S::as_mut_ptr()` as an integer).
82.     pub base: int,
83.     /// Distance in bytes between consecutive slots (`align_up(unit_size, unit_align)`).
84.     pub stride: nat,
85.     /// Size of each slot in bytes (the const generic `N`).
86.     pub unit_size: nat,
87.     /// Required alignment of each slot in bytes (the const generic `A`).
88.     pub unit_align: nat,
89.     /// Number of slots the pool can ever yield (`S::NUM_UNITS`).
90.     pub capacity: nat,
91.     /// Total size in bytes of the backing region (`S::STORAGE_SIZE`).
92.     pub storage_size: nat,
93.     /// Number of slots already handed out. The only dynamic field.
94.     pub allocated: nat,
95. }
96. 
97. impl BumpView {
98.     /// Address of slot `i` (0-based). The pool's geometry, independent of the
99.     /// allocation mechanism.
100.     pub open spec fn slot_addr(self, i: int) -> int {
101.         self.base + i * (self.stride as int)
102.     }
103. 
104.     /// A slot index is *consumed* iff it is below the high-water mark.
105.     pub open spec fn is_consumed(self, i: int) -> bool {
106.         0 <= i < self.allocated
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// The allocator still has at least one free slot.
110.     pub open spec fn has_capacity(self) -> bool {
111.         self.allocated < self.capacity
112.     }
113. 
114.     /// Well-formedness of the abstract pool. Each clause backs a caller-visible
115.     /// guarantee (see `view_design.md` section 3).
116.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
117.         // (a) Geometry is well formed: non-empty, non-overlapping slots.
118.         &&& self.unit_size > 0
119.         &&& self.unit_align > 0
120.         &&& self.stride >= self.unit_size
121.         // (b) Stride is the up-alignment of the unit size to the unit alignment,
122.         //     and every slot start inherits `unit_align` from an aligned base.
123.         &&& align_up_spec(self.unit_size, self.unit_align) == Some(self.stride)
124.         &&& (self.stride as int) % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
125.         &&& self.base % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
126.         // (c) The pool fits inside the backing region.
127.         &&& (self.capacity as int) * (self.stride as int) <= self.storage_size as int
128.         // (d) Addresses do not wrap the usize space.
129.         &&& self.base >= 0
130.         &&& self.base + (self.storage_size as int) <= usize::MAX as int + 1
131.         // (e) Monotone-capacity ceiling.
132.         &&& self.allocated <= self.capacity
133.     }

  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it

  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature

  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume

  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in

  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),

  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).

2. 
3. Genuine Verus front-end limitations encountered while specifying the in-scope
4. exec functions. Per the **verus-constraints** skill these are recorded here and
5. **not** worked around (no exec rewrite, no `external_body`, no
6. `assume_specification`). The affected functions are therefore left unannotated so
7. the crate still compiles under Verus and the remaining items (`align_up`, the
8. `BumpView` model, and the proof-lemma targets) verify with `0 errors`.
9. 
10. ## 1. `break` with a value (`break <expr>;`)
11. 
12. - **Function:** `FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` (`lib.rs:~265`).
13. - **Exact error:**
14.   ```
15.   error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
16.   complex break expressions
17.      --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:298:17
18.       |
19.   298 |                 break current;
20.   ```
21. - **Minimal trigger:** a `loop { ...; break value; }` that yields a value out of
22.   the loop (the CAS reservation loop).
23. 
24. ## 2. Raw-pointer materialization from an integer address
25. 
26. Two distinct front-end errors, both rooted in turning a backend-provided
27. `usize`/`*mut u8` address into a typed `&'static mut` reference:
28. 
29. - **`alloc`** (`lib.rs:295`, after the `break` is rewritten to a plain `break`):
30.   ```
31.   error: Verus does not support this cast: `usize` to `*mut [u8; N/#0]`
32.      --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:301:27
33.       |
34.   301 |         Ok(unsafe { &mut *(ptr as *mut [u8; N]) })
35.       |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
36.   ```
37. - **`alloc_as`** (`lib.rs:335`):
38.   ```
39.   error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
40.   dereferencing a raw pointer. Currently, Verus only supports raw pointers
41.   through the permissioned raw_ptr interface:
42.   https://verus-lang.github.io/verus/verusdoc/vstd/raw_ptr/index.html
43.      --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:335:26
44.       |
45.   335 |     Ok(unsafe { &mut *(slot.as_mut_ptr() as *mut MaybeUninit<T>) })
46.   ```
47. 
48. `vstd::raw_ptr` is the only supported route, and it requires a `PointsTo`/
49. `PointsToRaw` permission token for the memory. That memory is owned by the
50. external `BssStorage` backend (`S::as_mut_ptr()`); there is **no** permission
51. source for it. Fabricating one is exactly the unsafe `BssStorage` contract and
52. would require `external_body`, which is forbidden here (`bump_allocator` is not in
53. `tcb-allowed.md`). Therefore `alloc`/`alloc_as` cannot carry a verified body in
54. this phase.
55. 
56. ## 3. `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` value is not spec-readable
57. 
58. Attaching `BumpView` as the `View` of `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` requires reading the
59. dynamic `allocated` count from the `next_slot: AtomicUsize` cursor inside
60. `spec fn view()`. There is no spec accessor:
61. ```
62. error[E0061]: this method takes 1 argument but 0 arguments were supplied
63.     --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs:156:39
64.      |
65.  156 |     allocated: self.next_slot.load() as nat,
66.      |                               ^^^^-- argument #1 of type `Ordering` is missing
67. ```
68. `load` is an `exec` method, uncallable from `spec`. vstd confirms the limitation
69. in `vstd/std_specs/atomic.rs`:
70. > "This provides NO support for reasoning about the values inside the atomics.
71. >  If you need to do that, see `vstd::atomic` or `vstd::atomic_ghost` instead."
72. 
73. Reading `allocated` in spec would require replacing `AtomicUsize` with
74. `vstd::atomic_ghost` machinery (an `AtomicInvariant` carrying the ghost state),
75. whose value is openable only inside `proof`/`exec` `atomic_with_ghost!` blocks —
76. **not** inside a deterministic `spec fn view()`. So `BumpView` cannot be the
77. literal `impl View` of the allocator; the `v → v'` transition must instead be
78. threaded as a ghost token through `&self`. This is the proof-phase modeling work
79. the design doc (§7 "Modeling note") already defers.
80. 
81. ## Consequence

84. `alloc_as` cannot be body-verified in this phase; their intended caller contracts
85. are captured as proof-lemma targets in `lib.proof.rs`
86. (`lemma_geometry`, `lemma_exhausted_boundary`, `lemma_alloc_transition`) and
87. tracked in `verification-todo.md`.

 source for it. Fabricating one is exactly the unsafe `BssStorage` contract and
 would require `external_body`, which is forbidden here (`bump_allocator` is not in
 `tcb-allowed.md`). Therefore `alloc`/`alloc_as` cannot carry a verified body in
 this phase.
 
 ## 3. `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` value is not spec-readable
 
 Attaching `BumpView` as the `View` of `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` requires reading the
 dynamic `allocated` count from the `next_slot: AtomicUsize` cursor inside
 `spec fn view()`. There is no spec accessor:
 ```
 error[E0061]: this method takes 1 argument but 0 arguments were supplied
     --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs:156:39
      |
  156 |     allocated: self.next_slot.load() as nat,
      |                               ^^^^-- argument #1 of type `Ordering` is missing
 ```
 `load` is an `exec` method, uncallable from `spec`. vstd confirms the limitation
 in `vstd/std_specs/atomic.rs`:
 > "This provides NO support for reasoning about the values inside the atomics.
 >  If you need to do that, see `vstd::atomic` or `vstd::atomic_ghost` instead."
 
 Reading `allocated` in spec would require replacing `AtomicUsize` with
 `vstd::atomic_ghost` machinery (an `AtomicInvariant` carrying the ghost state),
 whose value is openable only inside `proof`/`exec` `atomic_with_ghost!` blocks —
 **not** inside a deterministic `spec fn view()`. So `BumpView` cannot be the
 literal `impl View` of the allocator; the `v → v'` transition must instead be
 threaded as a ghost token through `&self`. This is the proof-phase modeling work
 the design doc (§7 "Modeling note") already defers.
 
 ## Consequence
 
 `align_up` and the `BumpView` abstract model verify cleanly. `alloc` and
 `alloc_as` cannot be body-verified in this phase; their intended caller contracts
 are captured as proof-lemma targets in `lib.proof.rs`
 (`lemma_geometry`, `lemma_exhausted_boundary`, `lemma_alloc_transition`) and
 tracked in `verification-todo.md`.
